title: Cytocompatibility of Bone Substitute Materials and Membranes
authors: Schafer S, Al-Qaddo H, Gosau M, Smeets R, Hartjen P, Friedrich RE, Nada OA, Vollkommer T, Rashad A. In Vivo. 2021 Jul-Aug;35(4):2035-2040. doi: 10.21873/invivo.12472.
supports: Pre-clinical study from the botiss collprotect (porcine dermis) literature list — the product featured in it, which is not the same as the study being about the product, so check the design and the comparator before citing it as product evidence. Authors' conclusion, verbatim: “All examined bone substitute materials and membranes were found to be cytocompatible. In order to assess whether the observed minor differences can impact regenerative processes, further in vivo studies need to be conducted” This records what the paper says, not what a rep may say: the sales wording still has to pass the claim tiers, and a study in one indication licenses nothing in another.
